quarterly_data.signal: CEO Gary Dickerson walked through how the 2026 revenue forecast has been raised through the year: in February Applied said greater than 20% revenue growth, in May greater than 30% revenue growth, and now it is approaching 40% revenue growth. 80% of wafer fab equipment growth this year is leading foundry logic, DRAM including High-Bandwidth Memory and advanced packaging, and management sees that same mix in 2027 and going forward.
quarterly_data.figure: approaching 40% revenue growth (from greater than 20% revenue growth in February and greater than 30% revenue growth in May); 80% of wafer fab equipment growth

quarterly_data.signal: Structural mix shift at leading-edge foundry: a few years ago smartphone wafer starts were 4 times larger than data center, today they are one to one, and in a couple of years it will be two to one data center versus smartphone. Management calls data center versus smartphone the driver for the next several years.
quarterly_data.figure: smartphone wafer starts 4 times larger than data center a few years ago; one to one today; two to one data center versus smartphone in a couple of years

quarterly_data.signal: Pricing and margin: Semiconductor Systems gross margin is in the mid-50s and has increased about 190 basis points over the last year, with services margins up 180 basis points, and management has high confidence it can keep driving both higher because customer profit pools are larger than ever. On services, moving a customer to a different service contract can more than double revenue per tool, with over 37,000 chambers in the field connected to AI-enabled servers.
quarterly_data.figure: Semiconductor Systems gross margin mid-50s, up about 190 basis points; services margins up 180 basis points; can more than double revenue per tool on some service contracts

quarterly_data.signal: China / ICAPS: China is mostly ICAPS (IoT, communication, auto, power, sensors) for Applied. Applied is seeing growth this year in China and overall ICAPS and gaining a little bit of share in the areas where it can compete inside China, and expects that business to grow a little faster next year than this year. Near-term ICAPS growth is being driven by power in data center and photonics; longer term ICAPS grows mid to high single digits, slower than the AI data center segments.
quarterly_data.figure: ICAPS mid to high single digits longer term; China and ICAPS growing this year and a little faster next year

quarterly_data.signal: Capital allocation: Applied will return 80%-100% of cash to shareholders. Management said large M&A is not possible in the current geopolitical environment, so the company is doing smaller deals - the panel plating acquisition and an X-ray technology company - plus strategic investments, including hybrid bonding, where Applied is combining a partner technology with five technologies from Applied Materials on an Applied Materials platform.
quarterly_data.figure: 80%-100% of cash returned to shareholders; hybrid bonding combines a partner technology with five technologies from Applied Materials

quarterly_data.signal: First size disclosure for the advanced packaging business alongside the raised growth rate: packaging is forecast to grow over 70% this year with a midpoint between $2 billion and $3 billion in terms of the size of the business for Applied Materials. High-Bandwidth Memory and 3DIC are the fastest-growing segments this year. Applied's inspection and measurement business, both eBeam and optical, is growing over 50% this calendar year, and management is highly confident that in the next three to five years there will be incredible inflections in how computing components are connected.
quarterly_data.figure: advanced packaging over 70% this year, midpoint between $2 billion and $3 billion; inspection/measurement over 50% this calendar year
